move: two halves slide in to a seam, shift left to favour after
how: Left (grayscale, darkened) and right (saturated) panels of the same photo slide in from their own sides (xPercent ∓100, expo.out 0.8s, right 0.08s later) and a centre seam draws scaleY with expo.inOut; Before/After labels pop up with back.out(1.8). Both images share one slow push from scale 1.12 to 1.0 linearly. At 0.34D both panels and the seam shift left by 14% with expo.inOut so the after side dominates, an arrow pops in with back.out(2.2) then shrinks away, a stat card fades up and a caption rises from a mask. From 0.87D the caption and stat drop, labels and seam retract with expo.in, and both panels leave the way they came.
adapt: Swap the background image (both panels use the same URL with different CSS filters), the Before/After labels, stat text and caption; keep the 0.8s expo.out entrance and the 0.7s 14% shift beat.
port: mount(el, shot) builds .panel.l and .panel.r with .img, .lab, .stat, plus .seam, .arrow and .cap; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with offsets as fractions of D (shift 1.7/5, caption 2.3/5, exit 4.35/5). Scope selectors to el; the odd seam xPercent expression reduces to a fixed x:-90 shift.
caveats: grayscale/saturate filters on two full-frame images
the seam tween mixes xPercent and x in a confusing expression
from() on .stat after a .to on the same property; keep order when porting
